implementation_notes: A record is a transparent carrier of immutable data: its fields are final and its API derives mechanically from the header (JEP 395), which makes it the natural return type of a query and the natural input of a rule. Write rules as static methods returning new records, keep identity-bearing classes' transitions as void command methods, and use the unmodifiable factories (List.of, Map.of, Stream.toList) for results that leave the query. Java has no const or readonly, so the guarantee is convention plus final fields, and a record is only as immutable as its components - copy arrays and collections at the boundary.
pitfalls: A record is only as immutable as its components: an array or collection component can still be mutated in place, so copy it when constructing and when returning.
Accessors that initialise lazily or log turn the query into a command; records remove the fields you would be tempted to cache into, but identity-bearing classes still have them.

variants.name: final-field value classes with Stream pipelines (Java 8 and later)
variants.idiom_name: final fields and no setters; Stream pipeline without mutation
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-records realization a Java 8 codebase must write: value classes with final fields, a full constructor, no setters, equals/hashCode and defensive copies of mutable components; computation is expressed as Stream pipelines, which the JDK documents as functional in nature - an operation produces a result but does not modify its source - so a rule becomes a pipeline ending in a reduction rather than an in-place update. Choose it when the project's floor predates records or when the codebase already speaks streams; the newer variant changes the value carrier, not the pipeline.
pitfalls: Lambdas must be non-interfering and stateless: the stream documentation requires it, and a lambda that appends to an outer collection silently reinstates the side effect the pattern removes.
Collectors.toList() returns a mutable list; use the unmodifiable downstream forms or List.copyOf when the result escapes the query.
final prevents rebinding, not mutation: a final List field still refers to a mutable list.
